stem.text: A child of mass $20\,\text{kg}$ stands on the rough surface of a sledge of mass $40\,\text{kg}$. The sledge can slide on a horizontal frictionless surface.
One end of a rope is attached to the sledge. The rope passes around a fixed frictionless pole, and the other end of the rope is held by the child, as shown.

stem.alt: Child sitting on a sledge on a horizontal surface, holding a horizontal rope that runs to a pole at the right. Labels: horizontal rope, frictionless pole, frictionless surface.

stem.text: The rope is horizontal. The child pulls on the rope with a horizontal force of $12\,\text{N}$. This causes the child and the sledge to move with equal acceleration towards the pole.
What is the frictional force between the child and the sledge?
